controls.rationale: An undiscovered or unaudited accountable mutation may be relevant to whether appropriate event types are selected for logging.
Missing semantic audit evidence may be relevant to whether audit records contain sufficient event, actor, target, outcome, and context information.
A mutation path with no durable audit evidence may be relevant to audit record generation coverage.
A mutation can commit while its audit record is lost when audit generation is not durably coupled to the mutation.
Durability and protection of audit information are related assurance concerns, though transaction atomicity alone does not establish AU-9 satisfaction.
A privileged or permission-bypassing mutation without visible authorization evidence may be relevant to access enforcement.
When authorization decisions are accountability-relevant, AuditSpec can preserve the decision and its context in the audit record.

caveat: This profile is a relevance crosswalk only. AuditSpec findings and evidence are not control assessment determinations and do not establish NIST SP 800-53 compliance.
